transcriptText:
You got your chips in ahead... and lost. Did you play it wrong? Pick an answer first. Yes, you lost... or not necessarily?

Here's the hand. You've got ace-jack on a jack-high board. Top pair. Ace Andy moves all-in for five hundred... you call, and the pot's a thousand. Then Andy shows queen-nine of hearts. He needs a heart... a king or an eight for the straight... or a queen.

Now look at every card that could come on the river. There are forty-four. Twenty-six win for you... eighteen win for him. But this time, the river's the seven of hearts. He makes a flush, and wins this hand.

So play this same spot again... and again. A hundred players, all making this call. After one hand, forty-one are behind. After ten, eighteen. After a hundred, three. After a thousand? Basically none. On average, this call earns you about ninety-one chips a hand. Over a thousand hands, that's more than ninety thousand.

So... did you play it wrong? Not necessarily. Losing this hand didn't make the call wrong. Luck decides a hand. Skill decides a thousand.
